{{Short description|Czech biologist (1937–2021)}}
[[Engineer's degree|Ing.]] '''Jaroslav Mareš''' (28 December 1937 in [[Brno]], [[Czechoslovakia]] – 5 May 2021, [[Prague]]) was a Czech [[cryptozoologist]], biologist, traveller and writer.

He graduated from The University of Economics in [[Prague]], getting a degree of Ing (he studied international business). He worked for [[Czech Airlines]] in [[Iran]] and later in [[Canada]]. He visited 85 countries and organised several expeditions for research of [[cryptids]], such as [[Kongamato]] (for this he was offered the membership of the [[International Society for Cryptozoology]] which he accepted), [[Nandi bear]], [[Megalania prisca]], [[Bigfoot]], [[Yeti]], [[Nessie]], [[Ogopogo]], [[Champ (cryptozoology)|Champ]], [[megalodon]], [[Lusca]], Ambazombi and others. In 1978 he organised an expedition to the [[tepui]] which probably inspired [[Sir Arthur Conan Doyle]] for writing [[The Lost World (Conan Doyle novel)|The Lost World]] (a book based on stories told to Doyle by [[Colonel]] [[Percy Fawcett]]).

He also studied [[dinosaur]]s (he visited most of the famous [[fossil]] sites, such as [[Nemegt Formation|Nemegt]] in [[Mongolia]], [[Tendaguru]] in [[Tanzania]], [[Red Deer, Alberta|Red Deer]] in [[Alberta]], and other localities in [[Utah]], [[Colorado]], [[Montana]] and [[Patagonia]]) and corresponded with the world-leading [[palaeontologists]]. Another field of his interest was [[shamanism]].

In 1976 he discovered and later scientifically described the world's strongest [[carnivorous]] [[beetle]], ''Manticora imperator'', of the [[tiger beetle]] group. He became a specialist in this group of beetles and later described three more [[species]].

He published twenty two [[books]] and numerous [[magazine]] [[Article (publishing)|articles]]. He died in Prague aged 83.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-07 |title=Vzpomínka na Jaroslava Mareše |url=https://dinosaurusblog.com/2021/05/07/vzpominka-na-jaroslava-marese/ |access-date=2024-12-06 |website=DinosaurusBlog |language=cs}}</ref>
